 Search: SIGN UP LOG IN Press Release DC CELEBRATES WONDER WOMAN’S ANNIVERSARY BY UNVEILING THE YEAR OF WONDER
 BY: DC Publicity
 Tuesday, October 20th, 2026
 Legendary Writer Louise Simonson and Artist Cian Tormey Begin a New Four-Issue Story in  Wonder Woman  #41, Followed by a Six-Issue Story by Stephanie Williams and Elena Casagrande
 DC's Year of Wonder Begins January 20, 2027, with More Superstar Creators and Stories to Be Revealed
 Fans can celebrate Wonder Woman with a free-to-read selection of comics on DC UNIVERSE INFINITE
 Wonder Woman #41 main cover by Ryan Sook 
 B URBANK, CA , October 21 , 2026 — Since her debut in All-Star Comics #8 in 1941, Wonder Woman has stood as a champion of truth, compassion, and equality throughout the DC Universe and beyond. Princess Diana of Themyscira has lived many lives, but her commitment to peace and justice has never wavered. Today, on the anniversary of the Amazon Princess’s historic DC debut, DC looks toward her extraordinary future by declaring 2027 the Year of Wonder , an unforgettable year of stories from celebrated comic book creators. 
 Legendary writer Louise Simonson writes DC’s main Wonder Woman series for the first time beginning with Wonder Woman #41 on January 20, joining acclaimed artist Cian Tormey for a new four-issue story that establishes a bold new status quo for Diana and her world. 
 In Simonson and Tormey’s story, Wonder Woman is determined to abolish the Amazon Safety Act and clear the way for her sisters to return to the shores of Man’s World. But after everything they have endured, are the Amazons ready to return, or have they given up on saving humanity from itself? 
 “I haven’t written many books with female leads, and they don’t come any more iconic than Diana,” said Louise Simonson. “Teaming her up with Lois Lane, another iconic character, is a dream come true. Throw in Granny Goodness and her Female Furies? It doesn’t get more fun than that.” 
 Wonder Woman #41 variant cover by Cian Tormey 
 “Writing Wonder Woman , not just as part of the main series but during DC’s Year of Wonder, is both intimidating and exciting,” added Simonson. “Intimidating because my four-issue arc is sandwiched between the brilliant Tom King run and the work of the immensely talented, smart, and funny Stephanie Williams. Exciting because I get to work with artist Cian Tormey, who draws beautiful figures, exhilarating action, and subtle emotions with equal mastery. His pages are gorgeous!” 
 Following Simonson and Tormey’s four-issue story, writer Stephanie Williams and artist Elena Casagrande take the reins for an all-new six-issue arc continuing the Year of Wonder through October 2027. 
 Williams returns to Diana’s world after contributing four issues to DC’s Wonder Woman series in 2026 and co-writing Wonder Woman 2026 Annual: Wonder War – The Matriarch Special #1. She currently writes the DC GO! webcomic series Warriors and a Wee Wonder , which will soon transition to Warriors and a ’Tween Wonder . Together with Casagrande on DC’s main Wonder Woman  series, Williams will carry Wonder Woman into the next chapter of a year designed to celebrate the character’s enduring power, limitless potential, and place at the heart of the DC Universe. 
 “Diana has my whole heart,” shared Stephanie Williams, “so getting to come back to her world after Wonder Woman and Matriarch  feels like coming home, only this time with a longer runway. Six issues gives me room to really sit with Diana, to let her be fierce and funny and compassionate all at once, and to let the story breathe in a way I’m so excited for readers to experience. Plus, I finally get to work in the Nubia team-up I’ve been wanting to tell for a long time, but this time they won’t be going to Las Vegas .” 
 “ And I get to be in the main Wonder Woman series alongside Weezie? Louise is an absolute legend, and sharing this Year of Wonder with her is a full-circle, pinch-me moment,” continued Williams. “And then there’s Elena Casagrande, who is ridiculously talented. Few draw women quite like Elena does: gorgeous, powerful, and so full of life and movement. Getting to see her bring Diana and the Amazons to the page is a dream, and I can’t wait for everyone to see what she does.” 
 More Wonder Woman stories and superstar creators will be revealed as DC’s Year of Wonder continues throughout 2027. 
 Wonder Woman #41, written by Louise Simonson with art by Cian Tormey, features a main cover by Ryan Sook and variant covers by Daniel Sampere, Walter Simonson, and Tormey. The issue also features a foil variant cover by David Nakayama and a Sweater Weather variant cover by Alexander Lozano. The 32-page issue arrives at participating comic book shops and digital retailers on January 20, 2027, for $4.99 US, with card stock variants available for $5.99 US. 
 Wonder Woman #41 variant covers by Daniel Sampere (not final), David Nakayama 
 CELEBRATE WONDER WOMAN WITH DC 
 Readers can celebrate Wonder Woman’s anniversary with a special selection of stories available through DC UNIVERSE INFINITE. The Get to Know! Wonder Woman collection brings together defining adventures from across Diana’s remarkable history, with six comics available for fans to read for free on DC’s digital comics platform: Wonder Woman #1 (2023) by Tom King and Daniel Sampere, Wonder Woman #2 (2016) by Greg Rucka and Nicola Scott, Wonder Woman #226 (2006) by Greg Rucka and Cliff Richards, Wonder Woman: Steve Trevor Special #1 (2017) by Tim Seeley and Christian Duce, Wonder Woman #170 (2001) by Joe Kelly and Phil Jimenez, and Wonder Woman #51 (2018) by Steve Orlando and Laura Braga. 
 CITY OF BURBANK HONORS WONDER WOMAN 
 For fans in Burbank, the Wonder Woman celebration extends beyond the page. Fans can visit the larger-than-life bronze Wonder Woman statue located in front of the Warner Bros. Studio Tour Hollywood entrance at 3400 Warner Blvd. The statue, inspired by original artwork from acclaimed Wonder Woman artist Jenny Frison, offers fans a chance to celebrate the Amazon Princess and capture a photo with an iconic tribute to her enduring legacy. 
 Visit Burbank will also celebrate Wonder Woman on October 21 with a special comic book giveaway. Five fans will have the chance to win a commemorative Wonder Woman comic book, written by Amanda Deibert with art by Aaron Lopresti. Fans can enter by following @visitburbank and @dccomics and sharing a photo with the Wonder Woman statue. Follow @visitburbank for complete rules and eligibility; winners will be contacted by direct message on October 28. 
 City of Burbank bronze Wonder Woman statue 
 For the latest information on Wonder Woman, the Amazons of Themyscira, and the Year of Wonder, visit the official DC website at dc.com and follow DC on social media, including the official Wonder Woman accounts on Instagram and Facebook and the relaunched Wonder Woman Threads account, where you’ll see videos and posts celebrating Wonder Woman, including a look back at Wonder Woman throughout her publishing history, a reel highlighting Lynda Carter’s iconic portrayal of Wonder Woman, the rise of Absolute Wonder Woman, and more! 
 The DC UNIVERSE INFINITE digital subscription platform (DCUI) is the perfect place to discover even more Wonder Woman stories, including Williams’s Nubia & the Amazons , Trial of the Amazons , Nubia: Coronation Special , Nubia: Queen of the Amazons , Warriors and a Wee Wonder , and more. For more information and a free trial, visit www.dcuniverseinfinite.com. DC UNIVERSE INFINITE is not available in all countries and is not intended for children.
